analysis.one_liner: Polycab is India's largest wires-and-cables manufacturer, with a growing side business in fans, switches and appliances (FMEG) and a smaller EPC/EHV cable-projects arm.
analysis.whats_happening: Polycab reported Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sept 2026) results on 15 Oct 2026 - revenue up 53% YoY to roughly ₹9,899 crore and profit up about 43% YoY to roughly ₹990 crore, which management called the best quarter in the company's history. Separately, in mid-October 2026 the NCLAT stayed an insolvency petition a vendor (Asier Metals) had filed against the company over a disputed ₹2.79 crore payment; a final order is still pending. No results, AGM or dividend record date falls in the next few weeks - the FY26 dividend record date (19 June 2026) has already passed and the next results are expected only around mid-January 2027.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a cables-and-wires company that is also trying to build a second leg in fans, switches and home appliances (FMEG), and that second leg has just turned meaningfully profitable for the first time. Revenue and profit are both growing very fast - over 40% year-on-year. The tension is that the share price has not kept pace: it is down about 20% from its June 2026 peak and has only crawled up about 5% over the past year, even though profit grew far faster than that. That gap usually means either the stock was priced too richly before, or the market is discounting something else - here, an unresolved tax dispute and a (so far minor) vendor lawsuit are the likely suspects. At roughly 39 times earnings, the stock is still priced for continued strong growth, not for problems.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27: revenue ~₹9,899 crore (+53% YoY), EBITDA ~₹1,423 crore (+39% YoY) at a 14.4% margin - that margin is down from 15.8% a year earlier but up from 13.8% in Q1 FY27. PAT ~₹990 crore (+43% YoY). H1 FY27 revenue crossed ₹18,000 crore for the first time (+46% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 14.1%. By segment: Wires & Cables revenue grew 47% YoY with a 14.2% EBIT margin, at the upper end of management's own 11-13% long-term guided range; FMEG revenue grew 124% YoY and its EBIT margin crossed 10% for the first time, the segment's seventh straight profitable quarter after years of thin or negative margins. One flag: some media coverage attributes margin pressure to a roughly 60% jump in raw-material (copper) costs, while other reports describe copper prices as up only about 6% quarter-on-quarter - these two claims are hard to reconcile and the 60% figure likely reflects total raw-material spend (driven by volume growth) rather than price alone, so it should not be read as a pure price shock.
analysis.performance_read: There are no splits or other corporate actions to adjust for here, so the raw price series is directly comparable. The stock is 20.5% below its June 2026 peak of ₹10,083 and sits well above its 52-week low of ₹6,690. Over 1 year it is up only 4.89%, versus Nifty down 10.86% and peer Havells down 24.53% - so it has still beaten both, just not by much given the scale of its own earnings growth. Over 3 and 5 years the picture is much stronger: +55.55% and +246.87% respectively, far ahead of the Nifty (+17.88%/+25.07%) and Havells (-12.26%/-19.33%). The uncomfortable part is the recent gap between earnings (up 40%+) and price (nearly flat over a year, down over 3 months) - this is consistent with either a prior valuation re-rating down, or the market pricing in the tax dispute and litigation risk discussed below.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 38.7x and P/B of roughly 9.45x, the stock is priced expensively in absolute terms - this is not a cheap stock. Why it commands that multiple: ROE of about 24.8%, ROCE of about 34.1%, a net-cash balance sheet, and a newly profitable FMEG business that gives it a second growth engine. Whether that multiple is justified is a separate question - the stock trading well below its earlier price despite faster profit growth suggests the market has already become more cautious, likely reflecting the unresolved tax demand and the small insolvency-petition episode rather than any slowdown in the core business.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not just margin expansion. Wires & Cables revenue grew 47% YoY on genuine volume/market-share gains, and FMEG revenue grew 124% YoY while simultaneously becoming profitable for the first time (EBIT margin crossing 10%) rather than growing only through pricing. Margins did move - FMEG's inflection is real and durable-looking given seven straight profitable quarters - but the headline growth is coming from more units sold across both segments, which is the healthier combination described in Ticker Tales' own framework.
analysis.health_read: Financial risk looks low: the company carries almost no debt and is in a net-cash position (net debt/equity around -0.30, roughly ₹1,632 crore of net cash), with ROCE near 34%. Whether operating profit is converting cleanly into free cash flow is not verified here - check the cash-flow statement on Screener. The more relevant risk right now is business/governance risk rather than balance-sheet risk: an income-tax demand of ₹327.45 crore for AY2024-25 was cut to about ₹57.58 crore after a rectification order in March 2026, and the company is still appealing; separately, a vendor's insolvency petition over a disputed ₹2.79 crore claim was admitted by the NCLT before being stayed by the NCLAT in October 2026, with a final order still pending. Neither is financially large on its own, but both keep a governance overhang alive given the company's December 2023 tax search, which does not appear to have been cleanly closed out.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding has stayed broadly stable at around 61.5% through FY26, with zero shares pledged as confirmed by the company's April 2026 regulatory disclosure - a clean signal. The main recent change was a September 2025 block deal in which promoters sold about 1.5% of the company (roughly ₹1,740 crore at ~₹7,458/share) to institutional buyers including JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, HDFC Life and Kotak Mahindra Life - a stake sale, not a pledge, but worth noting as insider selling. Reported FII holding appears to have risen since late 2025, but sources disagree on the exact level (one cites ~14.2%, another ~19%); given the conflict, treat the direction (increasing) as more reliable than the precise number - this should be checked against the company's own shareholding filing before publishing.
strengths: H1 FY27 revenue crossed ₹18,000 crore for the first time, up 46% YoY, with growth spread across both Wires & Cables (+47%) and FMEG (+124%)
FMEG segment's EBIT margin crossed 10% for the first time in its seventh consecutive profitable quarter, turning a historically weak segment into a real contributor
Net-cash balance sheet (net debt/equity ~-0.30) with ROCE around 34% and zero promoter share pledge
Stock has beaten both the Nifty and peer Havells over 3 years (+55.55% vs +17.88%/-12.26%) and 5 years (+246.87% vs +25.07%/-19.33%)
watchpoints: An income-tax demand of ₹327.45 crore for AY2024-25 (later reduced to ~₹57.58 crore) is still under appeal, and its connection to the December 2023 tax search has not been clearly confirmed or closed out
A vendor's insolvency petition (Asier Metals, ~₹2.79 crore claim) was admitted by the NCLT and then stayed by the NCLAT in October 2026 - small in amount, but the final order is still pending
Despite 40%+ YoY profit growth, the stock is down 20.5% from its June 2026 peak and up only 4.89% over one year, a gap that still needs to close one way or the other
The EHV cable plant's commissioning has been pushed back from December 2027 to FY2028
analysis.one_thing: How the NCLAT rules on the Asier Metals insolvency petition and whether the income-tax dispute is formally and fully resolved - a clean outcome on either would remove a chunk of the current overhang; an adverse outcome would likely widen it.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT figures were cross-checked across multiple independent financial media sources and converged (revenue ~₹9,898.9 crore, PAT ~₹990 crore for Q2 FY27). Not verified: exact FII/DII shareholding percentages (sources range from ~14.2% to ~19%), the precise link between the December 2023 income-tax search and the March 2026 tax demand, the exact figure/year for the Project Spring revenue target, and the next quarterly results date (no official announcement found; mid-January 2027 is an estimate based on last year's pattern). Market data (price, returns, dividends) was supplied and used as-is without recomputation.
